findings.finding: Hybrid. (a) Software compounder: support $4.90B (-1% y/y), licence $0.66B (-15%), cloud applications (SaaS) $4.22B (+10%) in Q1 FY27; support is billed in advance, renewed by substantially all customers and priced as a % of licence fees. (b) OCI = compute capacity sold on 1-5 year contracts: $7.39B (+121% y/y), 38% of revenue (from 22%). OCI revenue = energized capacity x utilization x price per GW-year, but installed GW, utilization and price are NOT disclosed (only 850MW and >300k GPUs added in Q1 FY27): econ-review flags segment_unexplained (high) for Cloud and software (89% of revenue, 91% of segment margin). Segment revenue reconciles exactly to $19,345M; segment margin $10,255M reconciles to operating income only through unallocated R&D/G&A/SBC/amortization.

Q1 FY27 revenue +$4,419M (+29.6% y/y), additive by offering, residual 0: OCI +$4,041M (91%; structural: contracted capacity ramp), SaaS +$380M (9%; structural), licence -$111M and support -$60M (mix: legacy base flat to shrinking as workloads move to cloud), hardware +$104M and services +$65M (minor), FX < -1% (macro). FY2026: revenue +$9,957M (+17.3%), of which OCI +$7,867M (79%) and SaaS +$1,616M (16%). Americas gave 90% of constant-currency growth. Nothing in the growth is a price-cycle rebound; the risk is in who pays (next finding), not in reversion of a cyclical price.

RPO $664B at 2026-08-31 (+46% y/y, +4% q/q; ~9.9x FY26 revenue); per the 10-K ~12% of the $638B converts in 12 months, 34% in months 13-36, 34% in 37-60. The demand is concentrated and partly customer-financed: the 10-K says certain OCI offerings are 'more concentrated among a number of large customers', some 'highly leveraged'; press reports put a ~$300B five-year OpenAI contract at roughly half of RPO (attributed, not disclosed by Oracle; no customer was 10% of FY24-FY26 revenue). Q3-Q4 FY26 RPO adds were mostly AI contracts where the customer prepaid or supplied GPUs ($75B portion); Q1 FY27 brought $11.4B of customer prepayments with a financing component. Named buyers also include Meta and NVIDIA. The backlog's value depends on the credit of AI labs funded by outside capital.

Oracle builds ahead of revenue: capex $21.2B (FY25), $55.7B (FY26, 83% of revenue), $28.5B in Q1 FY27 alone (147% of quarterly revenue) plus $6.2B unpaid capex; $288B of data-center leases signed but not commenced (start Q2 FY27-FY29, 15-19 year terms) and $34.2B purchase obligations. The 10-K says lease terms 'typically do not align with the duration and pricing of customer contracts' (1-5 years). FCF -$23.7B in FY26 and -$5.4B in Q1 FY27 (-$16.8B before the $11.4B prepayments). Cloud and software segment margin fell from 60% to 55% (Q1 y/y) and 63% to 59% (FY); the incremental Q1 segment margin was 39% before R&D/G&A/depreciation already in segment cost.

STRUCTURAL for the forecast: the OCI ramp is contracted multi-year capacity (RPO maturing over 5+ years, take-or-pay-like with prepayments), and the software base is recurring support/subscription; Q1 FY27 operating margin 34.8% is inside its 6-year range (median 30.6%, max 37.6%), so no peak-margin run rate. The exposure that behaves like a cycle is counterparty and funding risk (AI-lab capital markets) and contract pricing after the first terms, which is a scenario (bear) lever, not a reverting cyclical price.

Conservative on near-term revenue and EPS, over-runs on capex. Ratio actual / guided midpoint: revenue Q4 FY26 1.005, Q1 FY27 1.013, FY26 1.005 (mean 1.008); non-GAAP EPS Q4 FY26 1.025 (ex gains), Q1 FY27 1.103, FY26 0.997 vs the Oct-2025 analyst-meeting $6.85; OCI FY26 1.006 ($18.1B vs $18B); FY26 cloud growth 39% vs 'over 40%' (slight miss); capex FY26 1.113 vs the $50B guide (first guided ~$35B per press). FY27 revenue guide 'at least $90B' (raised from $85B in Mar-2026, held in Sep), non-GAAP EPS $8.10 (raised from $8.05); consensus $90.4B / $8.14 sits just above. Long-term: revenue FY28 $130B, FY29 $185B, FY30 $225B; OCI FY27 $32B, FY28 $73B, FY29 $114B, FY30 $144B (guidance, not facts; 'most already booked in RPO'). quarter-review counted the capex over-run as a 'beat': it is not one.

GAAP FY26 EPS $5.83 carries the $2.7B pre-tax Ampere gain and Bloom warrant gains (non-GAAP $7.63 reported vs $6.83 ex gains): use ex-gain bases. SBC $4.81B in FY26 (7.1% of revenue) and $1.13B in Q1 FY27 is a real cost excluded from non-GAAP (non-GAAP operating margin 42% vs GAAP 34.8% in Q1). Restructuring recurs ($1.84B FY26, $94M Q1 FY27): kept as a cost. Q1 FY27 CFO $23.1B includes $11.4B customer prepayments (deferred revenue, not run-rate cash; do not annualize). Depreciation doubled to $7.6B (FY26) and will keep rising as $100B+ of PP&E and leases enter service. No restricted cash issue; spendable liquidity $37.1B vs debt principal $125.0B (net debt ~$88B before $34.6B lease liabilities and the $5.0B mandatory convertible preferred).

Piotroski 6/8 (mixed): fails no_new_shares and higher_asset_turnover. Altman Z'' 0.80 = distress zone (screen is weak for firms with buyback-depleted retained earnings, but here it also reflects a debt-funded asset build: total debt $129.5B vs equity $42.5B at FY26). Beneish not computable (Oracle reports no gross profit line). Rule of 40 not applicable. Every flag goes to the counter-thesis.

Capital allocation switched from buybacks ($20.9B FY21, $16.2B FY22) to building: buybacks $0.1B in FY26 vs SBC $4.8B, so SBC is no longer offset. Financing: $46.1B senior notes issued in FY26, $5B 6.50% mandatory convertible preferred (24.99M-31.24M shares on 2029-01-15), $20B ATM sold in Q1 FY27 (141M shares, $19.9B net); shares outstanding 2,880M (2026-06-12) -> 3,024M (2026-09-07), +5.0% in one quarter; diluted weighted shares +3.1% y/y. Plan: ~$40B debt+equity in FY27, no further bonds in calendar 2026 (release). Dividend $0.50/quarter kept. Incentives: the executive cash bonus pays on y/y non-GAAP operating income growth (excludes SBC and any capital charge); the field head's bonus on GPU / infrastructure / SaaS bookings; no ROIC, FCF or per-share metric. A securities class action (filed 2026-02-03, amended 2026-07-14) alleges misleading OCI statements.

ROIC (scores.roic, NOPAT / (equity + debt - cash), leases excluded): 25.6% FY21, 18.8% FY23, 16.6% FY25, 14.8% FY26; incremental FY21->FY26 3.4%; the numbers lane's year-end calc gives 12.8% FY26 (10.8% with leases) and incremental 6.4% FY25->FY26. Returns are above an ~8% cost of capital but falling, because capital (PP&E $7.0B -> $100.0B) arrives years before the revenue it is contracted to earn; whether OCI earns its cost of capital is unproven (no OCI margin disclosed; press says AI-infrastructure gross margin declined). Evidenced moat: switching cost in Database/applications support (renewed by substantially all customers; support still ~$19.8B a year) and multicloud Database growth (+404% y/y in Q4 FY26, sold inside AWS, Azure and Google Cloud). OCI has no evidenced moat against AWS, Azure and Google Cloud beyond available capacity and won contracts: it grows faster (+121% vs AWS +37%, Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82% incl. Workspace) from a base about one sixth of AWS, while those three spend 2-4x Oracle's capex on the same scarce input. SaaS (+10%) trails SAP cloud ERP (+25%) and Workday (+12.8%): no share gain evidenced in applications.

WARNING ROW ONLY (never a driver): in the Base Rate Book class of firms above $25B sales, about 4.1% grew at the guided FY27 rate (+33.6% nominal, 30.5% real) in one year and about 0.75% grew at the guided FY26->FY29 rate (40.0% nominal CAGR to $185B) over three years (class median ~2-3% real). Oracle's path is backed by $664B of RPO, which most of that class did not have, so the departure is explained by contracts, not by optimism alone; the contracts' counterparty quality is the open question.

flags: Altman Z'' 0.80 (distress zone): debt-funded build, total debt $129.5B vs equity $42.5B at FY26; net debt ~$88B at Q1 FY27 plus $34.6B lease liabilities and $288B of uncommenced data-center leases
Customer concentration: reports attribute roughly half of RPO to one ~$300B OpenAI contract (not disclosed by Oracle); the 10-K warns some OCI customers are highly leveraged
Duration mismatch: 15-19 year data-center leases vs 1-5 year customer contracts (10-K risk factor); re-lease risk if large customers do not renew
Negative FCF: -$23.7B FY26, -$5.4B Q1 FY27 (-$16.8B before $11.4B customer prepayments); no timetable for positive FCF (press summary of the call)
Dilution: $20B ATM (141M shares) in Q1 FY27, shares +5.0% in one quarter; $5B mandatory convertible preferred converts 2029 into up to 31.2M shares; buybacks ($0.1B) no longer offset SBC ($4.8B)
Capex over-runs guidance: FY26 $55.7B vs $50B guided (first ~$35B); FY27 $90-95B per press only
ROIC falling (25.6% FY21 -> 14.8% FY26) and incremental ROIC 3.4% (FY21->FY26): OCI returns on capital unproven, OCI margin undisclosed
econ-review segment_unexplained (high): installed capacity, utilization and price per GW-year of OCI not disclosed, so the revenue identity cannot be checked
Earnings quality: FY26 GAAP and non-GAAP EPS include Ampere/Bloom one-time gains ($7.63 vs $6.83 ex gains); non-GAAP excludes $4.8B SBC; Q1 FY27 CFO inflated by prepayments
Piotroski 6/8 fails no_new_shares and asset turnover
Legacy decline: licence -15% and support -1% y/y in Q1 FY27; SaaS +10% trails SAP cloud ERP and Workday
Incentives reward non-GAAP operating income growth and bookings, not ROIC, FCF or per-share value
Securities class action over OCI statements (filed 2026-02-03; amended 2026-07-14)
Outside view: ~0.75% of >$25B firms grew at the guided 40% three-year CAGR (warning row)

economics.reason: Growth is contracted multi-year capacity (RPO $664B, ~88% beyond 12 months) plus recurring support and subscription; margins are inside their own 6-year range, so nothing reverts as a price cycle. The cyclical-looking risk is counterparty credit, funding and renewal pricing of AI-lab demand, to be carried as bear-scenario events, not as forecast_options.cyclical.

type.override_reason: No override of the computed type, but it is a hybrid: the stalwart label fits the software/support base (~50% of revenue, flat to +10%); the OCI half behaves like a capital-intensive scale-up (revenue +121%, capex > revenue, negative FCF, external financing), and the valuation should treat it with scale-up economics (investment and dilution ahead of revenue), not with mature-compounder free-cash-flow assumptions.
